newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power up amid expected cold weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power up amid expected cold weather.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S., particularly the Pacific Northwest and Rocky Mountains, rose amid forecasts calling for colder weather next week, market sources said Friday.
"There is still a lot of hydropower around, but loads are going up so prices are too," said one Portland, Ore., trader.

Temperatures in the Northwest are expected to average 3-10 degrees below normal into early next week, while temperatures in the Southwest are expected to average 4-8 degrees below normal, according to Weather Services Corp.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Monday was quoted $16.50-17.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from $13.50-14.50.
Off-peak COB for Monday was also higher at $9.50-10.50.
Monday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was up at $16.00-$17.00, while off-peak was at $9.00-10.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Monday was quoted $19.00-20.00, up from prices as low as $18.00 for Friday.
Off-peak PV for Monday was quoted $9.00-10.00 per MWh.
Monday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were quoted $21.00-22.00, up from prices late Thursday in the mid- to upper teens. Off-peak Four Corners for Monday was quoted $9.00-10.00.
